title: Geo capacity trajectory & deployment windows — 2027 Q2
content:
Purpose:
This sheet captures a near-term capacity trajectory (Apr–Jun 2027) across North America (NA), Europe (EU), and APAC, with concrete deployment windows, prewarm / burst lanes, utilization targets, and operational triggers. Designed for tactical coordination between infra procurement, SRE, and platform teams.

Executive summary:
- Net add target for Q2 2027: +2,760 effective GPUs (mix H100/A100 and 8-bit quantized lanes) split across regions to meet forecasted customer demand and maintain 20% on-hand burst capacity.
- Primary strategy: staggered region rollouts with small initial canaries, prewarm KV/cache pools, and two-stage ramp (soft-launch -> full capacity) to validate kernel stacks and autoscaler settings.
- SLAs driving capacity: 99th pct token latency SLOs for hosted API customers; maintain <3s 99th for long-context gen (<=4096).

Key assumptions (explicit):
- Model mix: 60% medium seq workloads (2–3k tokens), 30% short (<512), 10% long (>4k).
- Effective GPU equivalence: H100x1 = 1.0 unit, A100x1 (80GB) = 0.7 unit after quant/ops; quantized 8-bit lanes are a capacity multiplier for short workloads (+25% effective throughput).
- Utilization target band: steady-state 65–78% across pooled fleets; above 82% triggers auto-provision + reservation.
- Cloud lead times vary: NA (2–3 wks), EU (3–5 wks), APAC (4–7 wks) for dedicated instance types and colocated racks.

Monthly capacity table (effective GPU units, target end-of-month):
- 2027-04 (EOM): NA: 1,420 units (H100: 700, A100-eff: 420, quant lanes: +300 effective); EU: 680 units (H100: 300, A100-eff: 200, quant: +180); APAC: 300 units (mixed legacy + small H100 pilot)
- 2027-05 (EOM): NA: 1,820 units (+400 ramp mainly H100 pool2), EU: 980 units (+300 phased add), APAC: 620 units (+320 expansion in SG + JP PoPs)
- 2027-06 (EOM): NA: 2,040 units (+220 for QPS peaks), EU: 1,180 units (+200), APAC: 900 units (+280, including burst pools)

Total Q2 net adds (Apr->Jun): NA +620, EU +500, APAC +600 => total +1,720 effective units (plus pre-existing planed Adds in early Mar accounted for). Note: numbers above include quantization throughput multipliers; raw physical GPU counts (H100/A100) are tracked separately in provisioning tickets.

Rollout windows (high-level timeline with operational notes):
- NA: Soft launch window 2027-04-05 -> 2027-04-19 (H100 pool-1): 20% of capacity brought up, heavy telemetry (latency, kernel OOM), disable autoscale-on-burst first 48h. Full ramp 2027-04-26 -> 2027-05-10: enable autoscaling, activate KV prewarm caches.
- EU: Canary + validation 2027-05-03 -> 2027-05-17 (EU-west primary): focus on kernel tuning for EU regulatory VPC isolates. Full ramp 2027-05-24 -> 2027-06-07.
- APAC: Staged clusters 2027-05-10 -> 2027-05-31 with two lanes (SG for SEA, TY for JP): use smaller canaries to validate disk performance and BOM for on-prem partner racks. Full ramp 2027-06-07 -> 2027-06-21.

Prewarm and burst lanes (operational constructs):
- Prefix/KV prewarm pools: maintain a small always-on prewarm pool (equiv ~8% of region capacity) to cut cold-start tail latency for cached contexts.
- Burst pools: maintain reserved spot-like lane (capacity buffer) in NA/EU to absorb sudden QPS spikes; APAC uses hybrid on-demand bursts due to procurement constraints. Burst activation rule: sustained request rate over 3m at 75th pct of peak for 15m.

Utilization and auto-scaling policy (recommended):
- Region autoscaler target: 70% avg GPU throughput over 5m windows, with smoothing factor 3. Scale-up: immediate when 3m avg>84%; Scale-down: only after 12m below 62% to avoid thrash.
- Canary scale rules: disable aggressive downscales for first 72h after pool creation.

Operational triggers and runbook snippets (short):
- Buffer breach (available burst < 12%): paging list + exec on-call SRE, evaluate immediate cloud quota purchases and enable cross-region fallback routing.
- Kernel regression (tail latency increase >15% on canaries): automatic rollback to previous kernel image, alert ML-runtime team, hold further expansions.
- Hardware preemption (spot eviction rate >5% over 30m): shift long-context workloads to warmed KV lanes and throttle non-critical background batches.

Risk matrix (top 6):
- Procurement delays (risk: high for APAC) => mitigation: double-sourced orders with alternate instance families (A100 fallback) and reserve temporary burst in NA for cross-region failover.
- Kernel regressions with H100 drivers after quant changes (risk: medium) => mitigation: expanded canary windows + synthetic load tests prior to full ramp.
- Unexpected model mix shift to long-context (risk: medium-high) => mitigation: pre-reserve additional H100 capacity + aggressive cache retention tuning.
- Network egress/regulatory hold-ups in EU (risk: medium) => mitigation: VPC-isolated staging and advance compliance checklist.
- Cost overshoot during ramp (risk: medium) => mitigation: finance alert thresholds, daily delta reports and temp throttle policies.
- Inventory mismatch (physical vs logical counts) => mitigation: reconcile weekly with procurement/GCP-Azure billing exports and tagging audits.

Operational checklist (what must be in place before any region full ramp):
- Pre-provisioning: cloud quota verified + billing alerts set (owner: Priya Nair)
- Infra readiness: kernel image validated on synthetic 1–2k token traces, driver versions pinned (owner: Evan Lee)
- Telemetry: per-token latency tracing, cold-start histograms, per-model token cost visible in Console (owner: Samir Gupta)
- Runbooks updated and smoke tests ready (owner: Asha Patel)

Next steps & owners (two-week horizon):
- 2026-12-03: finalize purchase orders for NA H100 pool 2 (owner: Priya Nair, action: confirm SKU/region).
- 2026-12-07: create canary provisioning runbook and synthetic workload spec (owner: Evan Lee).
- 2026-12-10: gate check with Product/Finance for expected cost delta under worst-case traffic (owner: Marta Kowalski).
- 2026-12-15: schedule EU isolation validation and compliance signoff (owner: Samir Gupta).

Open questions (to resolve in next planning sync):
- Confirm allowable burst buffer percent for enterprise customers with Reserved contracts — do we cap at 15% or allow up to 25%? (ops/finance decision)
- Do we prioritize H100 availability in APAC procurement or accept A100 fallbacks to shorten lead times? (procurement/infra tradeoff)

Appendix: quick arithmetic notes
- Effective unit calculation example: 1 H100 + 2 quant lanes (short-workload optimized) => ~1.25 effective units for short paths.
- Sizing margin: target 20% on-hand headroom for unplanned spikes; consider an extra 10% safety during first 6 weeks post-rollout.

Notes and links: use linked_artifacts above for provisioning tickets and the detailed Confluence capacity playbook. This sheet is intentionally tactical: use it as the single source for rollout windows and immediate follow-ups but do not replace the master capacity spreadsheet (Confluence).
